text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.66% today, a modest gain that fits within a broader two-week decline of 0.61%. The stock has been under pressure since hitting $424.89 on September 18, sliding roughly 8% over that span. The slight rebound today coincides with U.S. crude oil sitting at $96.41 per barrel after falling nearly 8% last week when Iran-U.S. diplomatic talks raised hopes for de-escalation; refineries are running at 94% capacity with healthy inventory levels (710.95 million barrels of crude in storage), suggesting the refining margin environment remains intact even if oil prices have softened.

The real headwind for the stock has been geopolitical uncertainty and conflicting signals. Last week's optimism from U.N. talks between Iran and the U.S. boosted the market, but Trump's rejection of Iran's conditional ceasefire proposal and reports of expected renewed bombing after the midterm elections have reintroduced risk premiums into crude prices. Refinery stocks like Marathon tend to face a squeeze in this environment—lower oil prices reduce profit margins on fuel production, while geopolitical volatility creates unpredictable swings rather than the stable, high-price regime refiners prefer.
